summary: LightLink is a python-based application designed to determine the time at which a spacecraft or lunar site will be in a suitable position to communicate with Earth, and whether it will have sufficient power to support its operations. Our project provides an interactive platform that analyzes Earth visibility and identifies suitable communication channels based on selected locations and time periods. Additionally, battery and solar-panel power analysis is conducted to help evaluate the energy conditions required for mission operations. We also integrated astronomical data from NASA Horizons and custom Python modules into LightLink which transforms complex calculations into accessible visualizations, charts, and tables. To conclude, this platform combined visibility analysis, communication planning, and power considerations with an aim to support a more informed mission planning while improving resource management and ensuring consistent performance in upcoming lunar missions.
details:
- Instead of treating each problem separately, our team integrated them into a single interactive application to provide a clearer overview of potential communication conditions.

- Complex astronomical and numerical calculations are converted into visual information that users can explore without needing to run individual Python scripts or manually interpret raw datasets. The application also supports different locations and time periods, making it useful for exploring various lunar mission scenarios.

 How does LightLink work?

Steps to analyze potential communication opportunities:

1.    Location Selection: Users select a lunar site or enter a custom location for analysis

2.    Astronomical Data Retrieval: The application obtains positional and time-related data, using NASA Horizons for astronomical information

3.   Visibility Analysis: The system calculates when Earth is geometrically visible from the selected location

4.    Communication Window Analysis: It identifies periods when visibility conditions meet predefined requirements. (minimum elevation angle = 5 degrees) and (minimum communication duration = 30 minutes)

5.    Power Analysis: The application evaluates battery conditions and solar-panel power availability

6.   Data Visualization: Results are presented through interactive visualizations, charts, tables which allow users to understand and compare the results

Factors Considered During Development:

  • Geographical Location: Different lunar locations can have different Earth visibility conditions
  • Time and Position: Communication opportunities change as the relative positions of celestial bodies change
  • Minimum Elevation Angle: A 5-degree minimum elevation threshold is used to determine acceptable visibility
  • Communication Duration: A minimum window of 30 minutes is required for a potential communication opportunity to be identified
  • Energy Availability: Battery conditions and solar-panel power are considered when evaluating mission resources
  • Data Reliability: Astronomical calculations rely on positional data retrieved from NASA Horizons

Technologies and Tools Used:

Programming Language:

  • Python

Framework and Visualization:

  • Streamlit: Used to develop the interactive web application
  • Plotly: Used to create interactive charts and visualizations

Data Processing and Numerical Calculations:

  • NumPy: Used for numerical operations and array calculations
  • Pandas: Used for data organization, processing, and tables
  • JSON: Used for reading and writing data files

Astronomical Data Retrieval:

  • NASA Horizons: A source of astronomical positional data
  • Urllib: Sends requests and retrieve data from NASA Horizons

Custom-Developed Python Modules:

  • visibility.py: Handles visibility calculations
  • earth_link.py: Evaluates potential Earth communication windows
  • battery.py: Handles battery-related calculations
  • panel_power.py: Handles solar-panel power calculations
  • make_data.py: Generates and prepares the data required by the application

- LightLink aims to make lunar communication planning more accessible and efficient. By helping users identify potential communication channels and examine energy availability, the application can support better decision making during mission planning.

- The project also provides a chance for future improvements, such as

1. Incorprating more advanced communication parameters

2. More accurate models that consider obstacles on the lunar surface

3. Detailed calculations to check the strength and reliability of communication signals
